content.title: Usher and Chris Brown tour: tickets cost, cities and what to know
content.text: Ads powered by ShowsSpotlightNEWSLETTERSearch the LatiNation websiteCultureEntertainmentMusicBeauty & FashionHealth & WellnessSportsHustle04.10.26 | HomeMusicUsher and Chris Brown’s joint tour could become the hottest R&B ticket of 2026Related ArticlesAds powered by Usher and Chris Brown have officially announced plans for their first joint trek, a stadium run being framed as the “Raymond & Brown” tour, and the reaction online has been instant. For R&B fans, this is not just another co-headlining package. It is two artists from different but connected eras bringing decades of hits, performance power, and fan loyalty into one event. Early reports say the full routing and on-sale details are still limited, but the scale already feels huge. That is why the buzz is landing differently. Usher is still riding the long tail of his recent live momentum, while Chris Brown remains one of the genre’s most durable touring draws. Put them together and this becomes more than a nostalgia play. It becomes a generational R&B event, the kind of show people will talk about before tickets even fully drop. Selena's Legacy Lives on at the Grammy Museum0 seconds of 3 minutes, 12 secondsVolume 0% Where is the Usher and Chris Brown tour going? So far, the strongest publicly listed stop is Charlotte, where Ticketmaster shows The R&B Tour 2026 at Bank of America Stadium on July 17, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. with both Usher and Chris Brown on the bill. That listing is the clearest signal yet that this is being positioned as a stadium-level event, not a smaller arena run. Beyond Charlotte, fans are already watching likely high-demand markets such as Atlanta, Miami, and Los Angeles, which have been cited in early coverage and speculation around where the biggest sellouts could happen once the full itinerary is released. None of those additional stops appeared fully confirmed in the official ticket listings I found yet, so they should still be treated as expected or buzzed-about cities rather than locked dates for now. How much could tickets cost? Official ticket prices have not been fully posted yet, which is part of why fans are already bracing themselves. Early coverage around the announcement has focused heavily on price anxiety, especially because a joint stadium tour with two major headliners usually pushes demand fast. Reporting on the rollout says final prices are still pending, but the expectation is that this will not be a cheap ticket. The clearest clues come from current market benchmarks. Vivid Seats lists Chris Brown tickets with an average price of about $253, while Billboard previously noted that for Usher’s recent tour cycle, resale tickets could dip under $100 but that many decent seats were more commonly in the $200 to $300 range, with premium inventory climbing much higher. That does not confirm exact Raymond & Brown pricing, but it gives fans a realistic sense of the zone this tour could enter once general sale begins. What should fans expect from the show? What makes this tour feel dangerous in the best way is the performance upside. Early reporting points to a stadium production built around big visuals, choreography, and a catalog-heavy set built for singalongs. The expectation is a night that blends solo eras with possible shared moments, rather than two disconnected sets under the same roof. That means fans will likely show up expecting Usher staples like “Yeah!,” “U Got It Bad,” “Love in This Club,” and “OMG,” mixed with Chris Brown crowd weapons like “With You,” “Forever,” “Loyal,” and “No Guidance.” In other words, this is shaping up like a full-memory concert, not just a tour stop. If the production lands the way the announcement suggests, this could easily become one of the most talked-about live R&B events of 2026. Argentine producer Amanda Szulansky, known as Zulan, made history on the Sahara stage by fusing club culture with the football identity of the South American country. Wearing the Boca Juniors jersey and featuring a closing set that included the National Anthem and the World Cup hit “Muchachos,” the DJ achieved one of the most deafening ovations of the day. In a festival known for high-fashion outfits and ethereal aesthetics, nobody expected the most viral moment of the weekend to come from a football jersey. However, the Argentine DJ and producer Zulan decided that her Coachella debut would not be just another set. Dressed in the blue and gold colors of Boca Juniors, the artist transformed the Sahara stage into a branch of the La Boca neighborhood, proving that Latin passion knows no borders when mixed with the best rhythms of global electronics. Selena's Legacy Lives on at the Grammy Museum0 seconds of 3 minutes, 12 secondsVolume 0% An epic closing with a World Cup flavor If the aesthetics were already striking, the end of Zulan’s set was what ultimately consecrated her as the revelation of the festival. In a bold move, the DJ closed her presentation with an electrifying remix that joined the chords of the Argentine National Anthem with the iconic “Muchachos,” the anthem that accompanied the National Team in its 2022 World Cup glory. The response was immediate, a sea of people jumping in unison in the middle of the California desert, creating a stadium atmosphere rarely seen at an event of this nature. “What pride,” Zulan expressed on her social networks, visibly moved by the connection achieved. “Proud to be Argentine and bostera. Thank you for sharing this video, I can’t believe it,” she added after seeing her performance flood digital platforms. Who is the DJ behind the phenomenon? Zulan is no newcomer to the scene. Raised between the United States and Argentina, she has successfully capitalized on her bicultural identity to create a unique sound that fuses house, garage and Latin rhythms. Under the banner of her latin dance proposal, she positioned herself as one of the freshest figures in the genre, with recent hits like Forever and Campeón (released in 2025) that already carried strong momentum before her arrival in Indio. Her appearance at Coachella 2026 represents a definitive turning point. By sharing the lineup with the biggest names in world electronics, Zulan brought not only her music but also a mix of original productions like Ricota and a sense of belonging that resonated with the massive Latin audience present at the festival. Identity and rhythm at the Sahara stage Zulan’s performance serves as a reminder that Coachella is a space where cultural identity acts as the most valuable asset. In an edition marked by the strong presence of Spanish-speaking artists, seeing the colors of Boca Juniors on one of the main stages stands as a testament to Latin “soft power” in pop culture. With her blend of summer house and football mystique, Zulan not only ignited the dance floor but also left an indelible mark on the festival’s memory. I understand I can unsubscribe at any timeAds powered by ;04.13.26 | HomeEventsMusicShakira and Beéle transformed Coachella into a desert Latino party with Afrojack and ShimzaRelated ArticlesAds powered by The hit “Algo Tú” by Shakira and Beéle reached the main stage of Coachella 2026 thanks to an explosive version by Afrojack and Shimza. The blend of afro house and Caribbean rhythms reaffirms the dominance of the Latino community in the most important festivals in the United States. Afrojack and the South African Shimza joined forces to globalize the Colombian sound in a historic edition of the festival in California. Music in the United States just experienced an iconic moment that nobody saw coming but everyone needed; specifically, Shakira and Beéle conquered Coachella 2026 alongside Afrojack and Shimza with a remix that transformed the desert into a Latino nightclub. During the Saturday set in Indio, California, the DJs surprised the crowd by dropping an afro house-charged version of “Algo Tú,” the track that the “She-Wolf” and the young Colombian talent released just this March; similarly, this collaboration proves that Latino pop no longer has borders and that the sounds of our Latino community lead global trends; consequently, both Anglo and Latino audiences vibrated equally with this fusion of gaita and electronic beats; in fact, the energy on the electronic stage ranked among the highest of the entire weekend. Selena's Legacy Lives on at the Grammy Museum0 seconds of 3 minutes, 12 secondsVolume 0% The sound of Barranquilla reached the hands of international DJs The success of this presentation at Coachella 2026 was no accident but rather the result of a commitment to globalizing Caribbean rhythms; therefore, the reinterpretation by Afrojack and Shimza at Coachella 2026 elevated “Algo Tú” to a level of massive exposure in the United States. Afrojack, an electronic music legend with Grammy awards to his name, knew how to detect the potential of Shakira’s melody to adapt it for the international dance floor; likewise, Shimza provided that South African afro house touch that is so popular right now, creating a perfect bridge between Africa, Colombia and California; in this sense, this version maintains the essence of the Caribbean while providing the necessary strength to rock any festival; for this reason, videos of the moment went viral within minutes. The impact of Latino culture on the largest festival in the United States This 2026 is marking a before and after for Spanish-speaking artists at the Empire Polo Club; furthermore, Shakira and Beéle indirectly joined the party led by Karol G in an edition of Coachella 2026 that screams Latino pride everywhere. With the participation of major urban genre stars and now these electronic fusions, it remains clear that music in Spanish serves as one of the main engines within the current industry in the United States; similarly, the union of two Colombian generations like those of Shakira and Beéle symbolizes the generational handoff and the strength of our roots; ultimately, Coachella is no longer just a rock or indie festival, as it functions more like the laboratory where the rules of the global game are dictated. In 2026, the Hall of Fame prioritized British rock and pop legends such as Oasis, Phil Collins and Iron Maiden. The absence of the Barranquilla native reopens the debate regarding Latin representation and the openness toward various genres within the Cleveland institution. In 2026, the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame sparked controversy once again. This Monday, April 13, the Foundation officially announced the eight artists for induction into the select music temple, and to the surprise of millions, Shakira’s name did not appear on the final list. Despite boasting a career spanning more than three decades and an indisputable global influence, the “Loba” did not clear the final filter of the expert committee, leaving the Latin community with a bittersweet feeling. Selena's Legacy Lives on at the Grammy Museum0 seconds of 3 minutes, 12 secondsVolume 0% Popular vote weight was not enough This year’s nomination was historic. Shakira competed shoulder to shoulder with legends such as Oasis, Iron Maiden and Joy Division. Support from her fanbase was overwhelming; the Colombian singer positioned herself firmly in fifth place in the fan vote, an indicator that usually exerts pressure on the final decision. However, the definitive verdict rests with a jury of 1,200 historians, artists and music industry members. Apparently, for this voting body, the cultural impact and versatility of the Barranquilla star, who has navigated everything from 90s alternative rock to global urban pop, must still wait its turn against more traditional rock standards. The Class of 2026 inductees This year’s list leaned heavily toward British nostalgia and 80s pop-rock icons. The eight artists who did achieve induction were: Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan. While the induction of bands like Oasis or Iron Maiden represented a long-overdue debt requested by purists, Shakira’s exclusion highlights the persistent difficulty Spanish-speaking artists face in gaining validation from high-prestige Anglo institutions, even when their sales figures and world tours surpass those of many selected. A wait that continues Despite this setback, the Colombian artist’s career remains at a point of creative effervescence. The fact that she reached the final nomination stage alongside figures like Phil Collins is, in itself, a recognition of her status as a living legend. The question now is not if Shakira will enter the Hall of Fame, but when Cleveland will decide to formally recognize that rock also speaks Spanish.
